Description: Password the browser interface (noVNC) asks for before showing the tool. Leave it empty and one is generated at the first start: it is printed in the console together with the interface address, and kept with the instance so it stays the same afterwards. Set it here to pick your own: it is applied at every start, and stays visible in this field.

Address the interface line should show: a domain name served by your reverse proxy, or your public IP, i.e. what your players will actually type. Leave it empty and the machine's own address on the local network is detected and used. It only changes the text printed in the console - the interface itself listens on the port declared in the Ports tab.
Placeholder: leave empty to detect the local address

Description: Steam account that owns Bannerlord. Needed to fetch the Coop dedicated server and Workshop mods: SteamCMD cannot download a paid game's Workshop anonymously. Leave it empty and the Steam step is skipped - the tool still installs, only the server files and mods are missing.

Used once, by the Steam step of Update. Clear it afterwards: Steam caches the session token in the instance, so later Updates work without it until the token expires. Never shown in the console output.
Placeholder: clear it after the first successful update

Description: Only when the account uses Steam Guard by email or app: the current code, typed right before clicking Update (it expires in about 30 seconds). Leave empty once the session token is cached.
Workshop item holding the Coop dedicated server. 3770450698 is Bannerlord Coop: its DedicatedServer folder is what the tool's 'Set server folder' button needs.

Workshop ids of the mods the server needs, separated by spaces or semicolons. Each one is downloaded and the folder holding its SubModule.xml is copied into server/DedicatedServer/Modules - that folder is the server's own Modules, so an Update never removes it. TAOM and the other non-Workshop mods are not on the Workshop: drop those zips into that folder by hand.
